vedic_reference.note: Kripānand is derived from the Sanskrit word 'कृपा' (Kripa) which means compassionate and merciful. The name is a combination of 'कृप' (Kripa) and 'नन्द' (Nand), where 'नन्द' (Nand) refers to the supreme God, Vishnu, who is known to be the giver of all pleasures and grants boons to his devotees.

historical_references.reference: Kripanand was a 16th century Nath yogi and poet. He is considered one of the most prominent Nath yogis in the lineage of Gorakhnath.
Kripanand was also a renowned scholar and philosopher of the Bhakti movement in India. He is known for his works in Sanskrit and Bengali languages, particularly his commentary on the Bhagavad Gita.
